text: 1. Say this to yourself in the morning: Today I will cross paths with meddlers, ungrateful people, the arrogant, the deceitful, the envious, and the selfish. All these flaws affect them because they do not know what is good and what is evil. But I have seen the nature of the good, and found it beautiful. I have seen the nature of the bad, and found it ugly. I also understand the true nature of the wrongdoer. I know he is my brother, not because we share the same blood or the same origin, but because he shares the same mind and a spark of the divine. Therefore, I cannot be hurt by any of them, since none of them can drag me into anything shameful. I cannot be angry with my brother, or cut myself off from him. We are made by nature to work together, like the feet, the hands, the eyelids, or the upper and lower rows of teeth. It is against nature for people to fight against each other, and what else is anger and disgust?

2. Everything I am consists of flesh, breath, and the ruling mind. Throw away your books. Stop distracting yourself, for you do not have the right to do so. Instead, act like someone at the point of death. Despise this flesh, this decaying bone and blood, this network of nerves, veins, and arteries. Consider, too, what your breath really is. It is just air, always changing, breathed out and breathed in again every single moment. The third part is your ruling mind. Think about this: you are now old. Do not let this mind remain a slave any longer. Do not let it be dragged around like a puppet by every selfish urge. Stop complaining about what fate sends you now, and stop dreading what might happen to you in the future.

3. Whatever the gods decree is full of wise planning. Even the workings of chance are connected to nature and woven into the designs of Providence. Providence is the source of all things. Beyond that, there is necessity and the greater good of the universe, of which you are a small part. For every part of nature, what is good is what comes from the nature of the whole and helps preserve it. The order of the universe is kept in balance by the changes of the elements, just as it is by the changes in the things they create. Let this be enough for you, and let these be your unchanging beliefs. Give up your thirst for books so you do not die complaining, but peacefully, with true and heartfelt gratitude to the gods.

4. Think about how long you have put things off, and how many times the gods have given you opportunities that you left unused. It is high time you understood the universe of which you are a part, and the ruler of that universe, from whom you came. A strict limit is set on your days. If you do not use this time to enlighten yourself, it will slip away, just as you yourself will, and it will never return.

5. Every hour, focus on doing what is in front of you with genuine dignity, kindness, freedom, and justice, just as a Roman and a man should. Free your mind from all other distractions. You can do this if you perform every action as if it were your last. Let go of all stubbornness, all passionate resistance to what reason tells you is right, and all hypocrisy, selfishness, and complaints about your fate. You see how few things you need to master to live a smooth, god-fearing life. If you hold to these principles, the gods will demand nothing more.

6. Go ahead, my soul, keep disrespecting yourself! The time you have left to respect yourself will not last long. Everyone's life is short, and yours is almost over. Yet you still do not honor yourself, and instead, you look for your happiness in the minds of other people.

7. Do outside troubles distract you? Make time to learn something good, and stop drifting aimlessly. But be careful to avoid the opposite mistake. Those who exhaust themselves in life with endless busywork are also trifling. They have no clear goal to which they can direct their desires and actions once and for all.

8. You will rarely find anyone who is unhappy because they did not pay attention to what was happening in someone else's mind. But those who do not carefully observe the movements of their own soul are guaranteed to be unhappy.

9. Always remember the nature of the universe, your own nature, and how the two are connected. Remember what part your qualities play in the qualities of the whole. No one can ever stop you from always speaking and acting in harmony with that nature of which you are a part.

10. When comparing different crimes, the philosopher Theophrastus makes a great point based on common sense. He says that crimes driven by pleasure are worse than those driven by pain or anger. A person overcome by anger is clearly pulled away from reason by a sudden spasm that catches them off guard. But someone who sins out of desire is conquered by pleasure, which makes them look weaker and less self-controlled in their wrongdoing. Theophrastus was right and truly philosophical to say that sinning for pleasure is worse than sinning because of pain. The angry person was wronged first and driven to anger by that pain, while the person seeking pleasure set out to do wrong on their own, led astray by their own cravings.

11. Do every deed, speak every word, and think every thought as if you could depart from this life at any moment. Leaving the world of men is nothing to be afraid of, if there are gods, because they would never bring evil upon you. And if there are no gods, or if they do not care about human affairs, why would I want to live in a world without gods or without Providence? But there are gods, and they absolutely care about human affairs. They have put it entirely in our power to avoid falling into true evil. If anything else in life were genuinely bad, they would have made sure we had the power to avoid it. How can something make a person's life worse if it does not corrupt the person themselves? The guiding force of nature would not have ignored these things out of ignorance, or known about them but been powerless to stop them. Nature would not fail us so completely that good and evil would happen randomly to both good and bad people alike. Death and life, glory and shame, pain and pleasure, wealth and poverty, all these things happen equally to the good and the bad. Because they are neither honorable nor shameful, they are neither good nor evil.

12. It is the job of our rational mind to understand how quickly everything vanishes. Physical bodies are swallowed up in the material world, and the memory of them is washed away by the tide of time. This is the truth about everything we experience through our senses, especially the things that trap us with pleasure, terrify us with pain, or get endlessly hyped up by our vanity. How cheap, how pathetic, how dirty, how fragile, and how dead they really are! Who are these people whose opinions and voices grant fame? What does it actually mean to die? If you look at death on its own and strip away all the spooky stories we attach to it, your mind will see that it is simply a natural process. To be terrified of a natural process is childish. In fact, death is not just a process of nature, but something useful to it. Your reason also shows you how a person connects to the divine, what part of them makes that connection, and what state that part is in when they finally reach it.

13. A poet once said that nothing is more miserable than a person who constantly wanders around, trying to dig into the secrets of the earth and guess what is going on in the minds of the people around them. They fail to realize that it is enough to focus on the divinity within themselves and serve it with genuine devotion. Serving this inner divinity means keeping it pure from passion, foolishness, and complaints about whatever gods or humans do. The work of the gods should be respected for its excellence. The actions of humans should be treated with care because we are all family. Sometimes we must even pity them for their inability to tell good from evil. This blindness is just as crippling as not being able to tell black from white.

14. Even if you were going to live three thousand years, or thirty thousand years, remember that you only ever lose the exact life you are living right now. You can only ever live the life you are losing in this moment. The longest life and the shortest life both end up in the exact same place. The present moment is exactly the same for everyone, and so what we lose is equal. It is clear that what you lose in death is just a tiny, fleeting instant of time. You cannot lose the past or the future, because how can anyone take away what you do not have? Remember these two things: First, everything moves in cycles and has been the same since the beginning of time. Therefore, it does not matter if you watch the same things happen for a hundred years, two hundred years, or for eternity. Second, the person who lives the longest and the person who dies the soonest lose exactly the same thing. They are only deprived of the present moment, because that is all they actually have. No one can be robbed of something they do not own.

15. Everything is just an opinion. The problems with this quote from Monimus the Cynic are obvious, but the usefulness of what he said is also obvious, as long as you take it for whatever truth it actually holds.

16. A person's soul disrespects itself most of all when it chooses to become an ugly growth, like an infection on the universe. Getting angry at anything that happens is a rebellion against the laws of nature, which hold together the order of all things. The soul also disrespects itself when it turns away from someone and deliberately tries to hurt them, just like angry people do. Third, the soul wrongs itself when it is overpowered by pleasure or pain. Fourth, it fails when it acts or speaks like a hypocrite, telling lies or pretending to be something it is not. Fifth, the soul disrespects itself when it acts without direction or understanding, throwing its desires and actions around blindly. Even the smallest actions should be aimed at a clear goal. The goal of all rational beings is to follow the order and law of the oldest and greatest community, the universe itself.

17. A human life lasts only an instant. Our physical substance is constantly changing, our senses are dull, and our bodies are meant to decay. Our soul is like a spinning vortex. We cannot predict our luck, and we cannot guarantee fame. Ultimately, the life of the body is just a flowing river, and the life of the soul is a hazy dream. Existence is a war and a journey through a strange land, and the only reward for fame is to be forgotten. What, then, can guide us? One thing, and one thing only: philosophy. Philosophy means keeping the divine spark within you safe and untouched. It means rising above pain and pleasure, living free from recklessness, lies, and hypocrisy. It means not depending on what other people do or fail to do. It means accepting whatever happens and whatever is given to you, because it comes from the exact same source you did. Above all, it means waiting for death with a calm mind, knowing it is nothing more than the dissolving of the elements that make up every living creature. If the elements themselves are not harmed when they constantly change into one another, why should anyone fear the change and dissolving of the whole? It is entirely natural, and nothing natural can ever be evil.
